rounds.text: Cheviot Company Ltd presents a compelling value case, trading at an exceptionally modest P/E ratio of 12.6x alongside a price-to-book ratio of just 0.93x [E1, E2]. Compared to broader sector benchmarks, the company's valuation metrics show deep discounting, highlighted by an EV/EBITDA of 0.35x and a P/E of 0.59x against sector benchmarks of 28.61x and 46.3x respectively [E6, E11]. Operational efficiency and profitability metrics further reinforce the bull thesis, with a robust ROCE of 21.37% and an ROE of 20.13% outperforming sector benchmarks [E9, E10], while maintaining an almost debt-free balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.01x [E38, E59]. Recent top-line momentum is clearly visible through a 25% compounded sales growth rate over the trailing twelve months and strong operating cash flows of Rs 42 Cr, accompanied by free cash flows of Rs 31 Cr [E17, E35, E36]. Furthermore, capital expenditure indicators show that CWIP stands at Rs 0 Cr, marking a 100% reduction that signals completed capital projects and incoming new capacity [E40], supported technically by a share price trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E50]. Conceded: compounded sales growth has been sluggish at -1% over 3 years and 5% over 10 years [E14, E16], and the DCF model indicates a negative margin of safety at the current market price [E46].

The fundamental engine of Cheviot Company Ltd is sluggish, highlighted by a 3-year compounded sales growth of -1% and a 5-year compounded profit growth of -7% [E16, E19]. This top and bottom-line decay translates directly to shareholder returns, with 3-year and 5-year compounded share price growth both languishing at -3% [E23, E24]. Furthermore, profitability metrics are uninspiring, evidenced by a low median return on equity of 8% over the last 3 years and a current ROE of 7.6% [E13, E28]. Valuation and pricing models also flash warning signs, as a discounted cash flow intrinsic value calculation puts the per share worth at Rs 996 against a higher market price of Rs 1128, creating a negative margin of safety of -13.2% [E45, E46]. Compounding these concerns, quarterly operating margins compressed by 3 percentage points to 12% in Mar 2026 compared to the year-ago quarter, alongside an inconsistent yearly margin trend [E31, E32]. Conceded: the company maintains a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.01x and trades at a price-to-book ratio of 0.93x [E2, E38].

Conceded: 3-year compounded sales growth is -1% and 5-year compounded profit growth is -7% [E16, E19], alongside a DCF intrinsic value reading of Rs 996 against a market price of Rs 1128 [E45]. However, the bear overlooks that trailing twelve-month sales growth has rebounded sharply to 25% [E17], proving that the medium-term top-line stagnation has broken. Conceded: quarterly operating margin compressed by 3 percentage points in Mar 2026 [E31], but the yearly operating margin actually expanded to 14% compared to 12% three years earlier [E30]. Conceded: 3-year median ROE is 8% [E28], yet the company's broader profitability metrics show exceptional strength, with an ROE of 20.13% and ROCE of 21.37% towering over sector benchmarks of 11.55% and 6.01% [E9, E10]. Furthermore, the bear's focus on past share price declines ignores that capital expenditures have largely completed with CWIP dropping to Rs 0 Cr, signaling new capacity coming online [E40], while the stock trades at an attractive price-to-book of 0.93x [E2] and near pristine debt levels of 0.01x debt-to-equity [E38].

However, this short-term bounce fails to erase a structural multi-year top-line decay featuring a 3-year compounded sales contraction of -1% [E16] and a dismal 5-year compounded profit decline of -7% [E19]. Conceded: yearly operating margin expanded to 14% compared to three years ago [E30], but the margin trend remains distinctly inconsistent [E32] alongside a sharp 3 percentage point quarterly contraction in Mar 2026 alone [E31]. Conceded: data provider metrics show high ROE and ROCE figures [E9, E10], but filed statements present a far more modest picture with a 3-year median ROE of just 8% [E28] and an actual ROE of 7.6% [E13]. Conceded: CWIP stands at Rs 0 Cr signaling completed capital expenditure [E40], and debt-to-equity is low at 0.01x [E38], yet borrowings actually increased over the year from Rs 7 Cr to Rs 9 Cr [E39]. Finally, pointing to a 0.93x price-to-book ratio [E2] disregards the reality that the market price of Rs 1,128 sits above the DCF intrinsic value of Rs 996, resulting in an unfavorable margin of safety of -13.2% [E45, E46].
